name: Givenchy
why: French fashion house with a couture history; menswear has shifted with each creative director.
origin: Founded in Paris in 1952 by Hubert de Givenchy.

onething.n: Shark Lock is womenswear — covered wedge, 3.5in heel. The 4G is a mark rather than a garment, and no menswear piece has survived the recent changes of creative direction

notes.fren: The Paris couture lineage is real and the men's line reads more international than that inheritance would suggest, which is why it scores four rather than five.

notes.craft: Givenchy PDPs state origin on every item checked (Italy for trousers, knit shorts and a leather bag; Portugal for a polo), with a traceability block naming countries of weaving and dyeing, but never a maker or mill. No owned atelier or factory is named on the site pages read. Country-of-make (with step-level countries) = 2. [audit proposed 2 at low confidence; held at 3 pending a second read]

cities: 8 stores, including Atlanta, Aventura, Beverly Hills · department stores, and its own site

marks: none found in 236 of 401 men's styles read. Zero named fabric or technology marks, house or licensed. Only generic lower-case descriptive prose: 'technical fabric' (5), 'water-repellent' (2). craft_evidence.owned_d: No owned atelier, workshop or factory named on givenchy.com pages read: careers page only redirects to LVMH recruitment; care-repair page mentions 'our repair workshop' with no place. No LVMH primary source on Givenchy-owned making was loaded (lvmh.com maison URL 404; a second LVMH URL hit the shared fetch-budget limit). So neither leather-goods nor ready-to-wear owned making is shown, and no group (LVMH) factory for Givenchy is evidenced in this run.
craft_evidence.countries: Italy 3/4 (cargo pants, knit bermuda shorts, Antigona leather wallet-on-chain), Portugal 1/4 (cotton polo). Sample of 4 PDPs (3 men's RTW: trousers, polo, knit shorts; 1 leather good, women's). No men's outerwear, knit sweater, shoes or tailoring sampled (sitemap excerpt did not expose those URLs).
